reason: Literary seam judgment requires connected text; the observation substrate is no_text by design. WEB USFM for Genesis extracted read-only (Strong's tags stripped to evidence-only clean text) for writer and reviewer roles.

defect:
Tier-0 USFM cleaner dropped same-line text following \p/\m/
b paragraph markers; 65 mid-verse continuation clauses were absent from the cleaned WEB working text (paragraph symbols preserved, content lost). Found by peer_crosschecker cluster 11-15 at Gen.39.6b; systematically enumerated by deterministic diff after fix.
impact_assessment: Verse coverage, substrate features, and OSHB extraction unaffected. Boundary decisions are verse-granular and paragraph seam markers remained visible, so span impact is expected to be low; content-reading impact is real and the corrected corpus is mandatory for all subsequent phases. One OL challenge (OL-M8-Gen-078-1) asserted a WEB rendering gap at Gen.35.22b that is actually this extraction defect; to be corrected in the boss ruling.
remediation: build_gen_inputs.py fixed to retain paragraph-marker same-line text; corpus rebuilt (Gen_web_clean.txt); defective version preserved as Gen_web_clean_v1_defective.txt; recovered-clause list retained in session records.
lesson_candidate: Cleaned working corpora must be validated against raw source by per-verse token accounting before review phases; a reviewer-facing corpus defect can masquerade as a source-text finding.
